label: 100m-m20slice
ticket: I1 step 3 - m20 buildable per row slice and mergeable
verdict: PARTIAL: every structural column merges byte-identically; one column (dtop, the Misra-Gries heavy-document candidate) is order-dependent and differs on 3 of 64,353 nodes. Blocked on a format decision, not a bug.
implemented: Builder::set_slice/set_first_row; close_one retains every node so a node whose occurrences fall in the neighbour survives; finish_slice emits a mergeable partial (ordinary node/edge columns at min_support=1 plus one 128-byte accumulator record per node: small[8], n, over, MG mg/mgc, 64 HLL registers); merge_slices decodes both partials, merges and re-emits through the same emit_node path; the shared chain is identified by path, counts add, children concatenate in code order, END accumulates, exact doc lists union in first-appearance order, HLL register-wise max on overflow, MG counters summed. counts stay per row (no row - start).

gates.a_product: PASS - rebuilt by the new binary: 87,192,432 B, sha256 eac582ca...f98bd (re-verified by the parent through gates/pfp_scale.sh, 4 workers, -m 2G, pin asserted)
gates.a_whole_range_payload: PASS 6,803,128 B equals the product's m20 member
gates.b_merged_member: FAIL on dtop only: nodes 64,353 == 64,353, edges 1,642,415 == 1,642,415, payload 6,803,128 == 6,803,128; nedge/ncount/ecode/echild/ecount/dndocs/dfirst/nfixed have 0 differing entries; dtop differs on 3 nodes (31303: 6580 vs 1937, 31323: 6580 vs 1937, 31524: 4581 vs 1937), all three overflowed estimators, first differing byte 6,076,288

why: dtop stores the Misra-Gries heavy-document CANDIDATE. MG with decrements is order-dependent, so summing two halves' counters cannot reproduce the single pass's candidate once a node overflows. Everything the merge can reconstruct is already exact.
decision_needed: A: keep m20 single-threaded in I1 - the writers split (proven) and m20 stays one stage, so the emission floor is the m20 feed (~3,000 s at 10 GB) and I1 gives about 2x, with I3 (cheaper feed) as the next lever.

B: make dtop order-independent so slices merge exactly. That changes the m20 member bytes, i.e. the container format and every existing v10 pin, and needs operator approval; the historical reference products could no longer be compared.
open_risks: a half-range partial is 3.86 GB (128 B/node of accumulator) against a 6.8 MB member, and merge_slices holds both trees resident: the accumulator must be trimmed (HLL + MG only for overflow nodes) before a K-range chain is pipeline-viable
only two ranges emit a member today; a middle group cannot yet emit a partial, so K>2 needs the assembler
